controls.statement: One authoritative source repository is identified.
controls.primary_reason: An authenticated project record can identify exactly one repository as authoritative for the assessed source scope.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The assessed project record identifies exactly one authoritative source repository.

controls.statement: Protected branches prevent unreviewed direct changes.
controls.primary_reason: Authoritative repository rules can be queried to prove that every protected target branch rejects direct changes lacking a recorded review.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every in-scope protected branch requires a recorded approving review before a direct change can land.
No configured branch-rule bypass permits an unreviewed direct change for the assessed principals.

controls.statement: Review cannot be bypassed silently by administrators.
controls.primary_reason: Complete administrator bypass settings and immutable audit behavior can be checked against versioned repository-platform semantics.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every administrator review-bypass path emits an immutable attributable audit event.
No administrator can disable or erase review-bypass recording within the assessed repository control plane.

controls.statement: Merge requirements include the required automated checks.
controls.primary_reason: A versioned required-check policy can be compared exactly with the merge requirements on every in-scope target branch.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every automated check required by the selected policy is a mandatory merge condition on each in-scope branch.

controls.statement: Changes are traceable from requirement or issue to code, review, build, artifact, and deployment.
controls.primary_reason: Authenticated identifiers can join the complete change inventory to issue, review, build, artifact, and deployment records without interpretation.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every in-scope change links to an authenticated requirement or issue and review record.
Every in-scope change links through build provenance to an immutable artifact digest.
Every deployed in-scope artifact digest links to its deployment record.

controls.statement: Commit history and release tags are protected against unauthorized rewriting.
controls.primary_reason: Repository ref-protection configuration and authorized principal lists objectively determine whether commits and release tags can be rewritten.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: All in-scope protected branches and release-tag namespaces reject rewriting by unauthorized principals.

controls.statement: Secret scanning covers current changes and repository history.
controls.primary_reason: Versioned secret-scanner execution evidence can prove coverage of both the current change set and every reachable historical revision.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: A versioned secret scanner successfully analyzed the complete current change set.
A versioned secret scanner successfully analyzed the complete reachable repository history for the assessed revision.

controls.statement: Departed personnel and obsolete automation identities no longer have access.
controls.primary_reason: Authoritative personnel and automation lifecycle records can be joined to the complete repository-principal inventory to find remaining access.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: No repository principal mapped to a departed person retains repository access.
No automation identity marked obsolete in the authoritative lifecycle record retains repository access.

controls.statement: Builds run from reviewed source.
controls.primary_reason: Build provenance can bind every build input revision to an authenticated review status for that exact source revision.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every assessed build provenance record identifies the exact source revision used.
Every identified build source revision has the review evidence required by the selected branch policy.

controls.statement: Builds are automated and repeatable.
controls.primary_reason: Authenticated build records prove automated execution, and a sealed repeated-build protocol can compare outputs using the approved equivalence policy.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every assessed build was executed by the declared automated build system.
Repeated builds from identical declared inputs satisfy the versioned output-equivalence policy.

controls.statement: A clean build produces equivalent output from the same declared inputs.
controls.primary_reason: A sealed clean-build experiment with a named equivalence policy can repeatedly compare outputs from the exact same declared inputs.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: A clean repeated build from identical declared inputs satisfies the approved output-equivalence predicate.

controls.statement: Builds fail closed when required verification cannot run.
controls.primary_reason: The approved verification inventory and CI outcome rules can prove that unavailable mandatory checks block rather than permit a build.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every verification required by the selected policy is represented in the build gate.
An unavailable, errored, or missing required verification produces a non-passing build outcome.

controls.statement: The production artifact is built once and promoted, not independently rebuilt in each environment.
controls.primary_reason: Build provenance and environment deployment records can prove that one immutable digest is promoted without environment-specific rebuilding.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The production release has exactly one build provenance record for its immutable artifact digest.
Every promoted environment records the same artifact digest and no independent rebuild provenance.

controls.statement: Deployable artifacts are immutable.
controls.primary_reason: Registry metadata and a bounded mutation check can determine whether every deployable artifact digest is immutable after publication.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every deployable artifact is addressed by immutable digest and rejects replacement of content at that identity.

controls.statement: Every artifact has a cryptographic digest.
controls.primary_reason: A complete artifact inventory can be checked mechanically for a valid cryptographic digest bound to each artifact's exact bytes.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every in-scope artifact has a valid cryptographic digest that matches its exact bytes.

controls.statement: Build provenance records source, builder, inputs, commands or workflow, time, and output digest.
controls.primary_reason: The explicitly listed provenance fields and their artifact binding can be validated without judging build quality.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every build provenance record contains source, builder, complete declared inputs, commands or workflow, time, and output digest.
The provenance output digest matches the exact assessed artifact bytes.

controls.statement: Artifact signatures or attestations are verified before deployment.
controls.primary_reason: Cryptographic verification results and deployment event ordering objectively show whether a valid signature or attestation was checked first.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Each deployed artifact has a valid signature or attestation under the selected trust policy.
Successful signature or attestation verification precedes the corresponding deployment event.

controls.statement: Build and signing keys are stored outside source code and build output.
controls.primary_reason: An authoritative key inventory and complete source and artifact inventories can prove the configured storage location and absence of known key material.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every build or signing key in the authoritative inventory is stored in an approved external key or secret store.
No inventoried build or signing private-key material occurs in the complete assessed source or build outputs.

controls.statement: Untrusted contribution workflows cannot access production secrets.
controls.primary_reason: Trust classification, workflow permissions, secret bindings, and a bounded untrusted-run test can prove that production secrets are unavailable.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every workflow triggered by an untrusted contribution has no configured production-secret binding.
A bounded untrusted-contribution execution cannot read any production secret in the authoritative secret inventory.

controls.statement: Pull-request builds cannot overwrite trusted release artifacts.
controls.primary_reason: Registry permissions and an isolated pull-request build attempt can prove that untrusted build identities cannot replace trusted artifacts.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Pull-request build identities lack overwrite permission for every trusted release artifact namespace.
A bounded pull-request build cannot overwrite an existing trusted release artifact.

controls.statement: Pipeline definitions receive the same review protection as application code.
controls.primary_reason: Path coverage and repository review rules can be compared exactly to prove equal protection for pipeline and application definitions.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Pipeline-definition paths are covered by review requirements at least as strong as the application-code paths in the selected policy.

controls.statement: Required unit, integration, security, policy, and packaging checks cannot be skipped silently.
controls.primary_reason: A complete required-check policy, merge-gate settings, and audit behavior can prove that missing or bypassed checks never become silent success.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every required unit, integration, security, policy, and packaging check is enforced by the protected merge or release gate.
Every allowed bypass of a required check creates an immutable attributable non-success or exception record.

controls.statement: Failed or canceled checks cannot be misrepresented as passed.
controls.primary_reason: A bounded matrix of failed, canceled, missing, and successful jobs can verify the CI aggregator's exact reported status.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Failed, canceled, and missing required checks never produce a passed aggregate build or release status.

controls.statement: Artifact registries enforce authentication, authorization, immutability, and retention.
controls.primary_reason: Registry configuration and conformance queries can test authentication, authorization, immutability, and the approved retention policy independently.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every in-scope artifact registry requires authenticated access according to the selected access policy.
Every in-scope artifact registry enforces the selected authorization and immutability policy.
Every in-scope artifact registry enforces the versioned project retention policy.

controls.statement: The previous known-good artifact remains available.
controls.primary_reason: The approved known-good release record identifies an immutable digest whose current availability can be queried directly from the registry.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: An authenticated release record identifies the previous known-good artifact digest.
The identified previous known-good artifact digest is currently retrievable from an approved registry.

controls.statement: Build caches cannot substitute unverified or cross-trust artifacts.
controls.primary_reason: Versioned trust zones, cache-key provenance, integrity checks, and an adversarial cache test can decide the stated substitution property.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every build-cache input is bound to verified integrity metadata and its declared trust zone.
A bounded unverified or cross-trust cache substitution attempt is rejected.

controls.statement: Release tags, artifacts, provenance, and deployment records agree.
controls.primary_reason: Immutable identifiers and digests allow an exact join and equality comparison across tags, artifacts, provenance, and deployments.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Each release tag resolves to the source revision recorded in its build provenance.
Each provenance output digest equals the corresponding release artifact digest.
Each deployment record names the same artifact digest as its release artifact and provenance.

controls.statement: Generate an SBOM for every released application artifact.
controls.primary_reason: A complete released-artifact inventory can be joined by digest to a valid SBOM record for every application artifact.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every released application artifact digest has exactly one valid bound SBOM record.

controls.statement: Include direct and transitive components.
controls.primary_reason: The complete dependency graph and final artifact inventory can be compared with the SBOM to detect missing direct or transitive components.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The SBOM includes every direct and transitive component found in the authoritative dependency graph and final artifact inventory.

controls.statement: Include runtime, operating-system, container, client, server, plugin, model, and embedded components as applicable.
controls.primary_reason: Applicability for each listed component class can be derived from complete artifact and deployment inventories, then compared to the SBOM.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every applicable runtime, operating-system, container, client, server, plugin, model, and embedded component appears in the bound SBOM.

controls.statement: Distinguish build-only, development-only, optional, and runtime dependencies.
controls.primary_reason: Authoritative package metadata and build graphs can assign the listed dependency scopes and verify that the SBOM preserves them.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every SBOM dependency is classified as build-only, development-only, optional, runtime, or another explicitly supported non-overlapping scope.

controls.statement: Record exact versions, package identifiers, sources, hashes, and relationships.
controls.primary_reason: Each explicitly listed SBOM field and dependency relationship has a machine-readable value that can be checked against authoritative metadata.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every SBOM component records its exact version, package identifier, source, and hash.
Every SBOM dependency relationship matches the authoritative dependency and artifact graph.

controls.statement: Link the SBOM to the released artifact digest.
controls.primary_reason: The SBOM subject identifier can be compared exactly with the cryptographic digest of the released artifact bytes.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Each SBOM names a subject digest equal to the digest of its exact released artifact.

controls.statement: Verify the SBOM against the final packaged artifact.
controls.primary_reason: A bounded artifact parser can compare the final packaged contents and dependency graph with the bound SBOM without source-only assumptions.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The bound SBOM component inventory matches the complete supported inventory extracted from the final packaged artifact.

controls.statement: Ensure no unexpected undeclared components are present.
controls.primary_reason: A complete final-artifact component inventory can be differenced against the declared bound SBOM, with unsupported formats returning Blocked.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: No component extracted from the complete supported final-artifact inventory is absent from the bound SBOM declaration.

controls.statement: Remove unsupported and end-of-life dependencies.
controls.primary_reason: A complete component inventory can be joined to authoritative publisher and registry lifecycle records for support and end-of-life status.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: No component in the complete dependency inventory is marked unsupported or end-of-life by its authoritative lifecycle source for the assessed version.

controls.statement: Check whether dependencies come from intended publishers and registries.
controls.primary_reason: An approved publisher and registry policy can be compared exactly with locked dependency identities and authoritative registry metadata.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every dependency resolves from a registry allowed by the versioned project policy.
Every dependency publisher identity matches the publisher allowed by the versioned project policy and authoritative registry metadata.

controls.statement: Monitor upstream security advisories.
controls.primary_reason: The complete dependency inventory and approved advisory-source policy can be compared to authenticated subscription and ingestion records.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every dependency ecosystem in scope is covered by at least one approved upstream advisory source.
Each approved advisory source has a current successful monitoring or ingestion record.

controls.statement: Continuously scan released components for newly disclosed vulnerabilities.
controls.primary_reason: Released component inventories and authenticated event-driven or policy-cadenced scan records can prove continuing vulnerability coverage.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every supported released component remains registered with the approved vulnerability-monitoring service.
Newly disclosed vulnerability data triggers or is included within the approved maximum scan cadence for every supported release.

controls.statement: Document ownership of vendored, forked, or internally patched components.
controls.primary_reason: A complete component inventory can be joined exactly to authenticated ownership records for each vendored, forked, or patched component.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every vendored, forked, or internally patched component in the complete inventory has a current authenticated owner record.

controls.statement: Retain SBOMs for historical releases and incident investigation.
controls.primary_reason: Historical release and incident inventories can be compared exactly with retained digest-bound SBOM records under the approved retention policy.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every historical release required by the retention policy has a retrievable SBOM bound to its artifact digest.
Every incident-required SBOM remains retrievable for the incident investigation retention period.
